head: e9e35067fc3b419a54d790a71663071455f203f1
purpose: Process-local GPU lifecycle and standalone C delivery with proving regressions
result: Qualified on the explicitly authorized desktop RTX 5080; the broader GPU proving goal remains incomplete

native_lifecycle.startup_cleanup: Only retire an engine created by the failed or panicking startup
native_lifecycle.shutdown: Reject retained sessions/commitments; preserve GPU selection; idempotent after cleanup

standalone_c.trace_handoff: Public values only; zero private trace readback

regressions.other: Retains candidate wallets, quotients/FRI, recursive sessions, worker admission and checked completion

build_checks: five static libraries and standalone C callers
pilot_notes: Original debug lifecycle pilots passed. An initial C pilot used underscore policy spelling and rejected before GPU allocation; corrected pilots passed ten complete C proofs.
Review identified missing live-device-selector validation. The engine now rejects a changed UUID or OpenCL index before allocation; current-source debug pilots passed.
The earlier laptop wide-release run passed 173 Rust executions but predates the selector fix and is superseded.
Run-02 archived current source/binary but ran no tests: the laptop disappeared before the device snapshot. Its failure log remains intact.
The user confirmed this is now a desktop RTX 5080 system. Run-03 explicitly targets its UUID and keeps historical laptop evidence separate.
The desktop runner also enforces lifecycle-marker errors and C++ header failure as qualification failures.
limitations: Application/Zig startup integration is not implemented by adding the native lifecycle exports.
Complete batch proofs remain qualified only through four padded tiles; 64-tile trace/root assembly does not qualify complete 64-tile proving.
Private worker admission, tree/recursive native delivery, quadratic lookups where required, owned multi-AIR commitments and full-size recursion remain open.
Strict release proofs cover the explicitly selected complete GPU path; debug proofs retain CPU constraint audits, and host orchestration/serialization remain on CPU.
Correctness qualification does not establish sustained transactions per hour, multi-GPU scaling, AMD or Metal results.
Pending Apple source still requires its authorized local Mac checkpoint commit; no SSH retrieval was attempted.
